svg.title: Dynamic Programming
svg.desc: Dynamic Programming. Solve each overlapping subproblem once and reuse its answer, top-down with memoization or bottom-up with a table. Step 1, Same subproblems, again: Naive best(6) makes 24 calls for 7 amounts: best(0) runs 9 times, best(1) 6 and best(2) 4. Step 2, Top-down: memoize: With a memo, each amount is computed once; the other 7 calls just read it. 7 computations, not 24. Step 3, Bottom-up: fill a table: dp[0] = 0, then each dp[n] = 1 + the least of the cells 1, 3 and 4 back. dp[6] = 2, from 3 + 3. Step 4, Spot it, then table it: Same recipe, new problem: the kitten → sitting grid fills to 3 edits: k → s, e → i and insert g.

g.text: Naive best(6) makes 24 calls for 7 amounts: best(0) runs 9 times, best(1) 6 and best(2) 4.
With a memo, each amount is computed once; the other 7 calls just read it. 7 computations, not 24.
dp[0] = 0, then each dp[n] = 1 + the least of the cells 1, 3 and 4 back. dp[6] = 2, from 3 + 3.
Same recipe, new problem: the kitten → sitting grid fills to 3 edits: k → s, e → i and insert g.
17 of 24 calls redo an amount already solved
7 computed, 7 memo reads: 10 calls never happen
each amount once: O(amount × coins) time

g.text: dp[n] = fewest coins that make n
dp[0] = 0 (zero coins make 0: the base case)
3 coins: took 4 first, never looked back
d(i, j): edits from i letters to j
d(i, 0) = i and d(0, j) = j
row by row, left to right
then read the last cell and trace back
diff = 0 if the two letters match, else 1
